sections.title: Times Between H and H+1 When Hands Coincide, Are Opposite, or Form a Right Angle
sections.content:
1. Coincide Time: Time after H o'clock = (60H) / 11 minutes
Example: After 5 o'clock
= (60×5)/11 = 300/11 = 27 3/11 minutes
So, the hands will coincide at 5:27 3/11.

2. Opposite (180°): Time = (60H ± 360) / 11
Example: After 4 o'clock
= (60×4 + 360)/11 = 600/11 = 54 6/11 minutes
So, the time is 4:54 6/11.

3. Right Angle (90°): Time = (60H ± 180) / 11
Example: After 3 o'clock
= (180 + 180)/11 = 360/11 = 32 8/11 minutes

3–4 Step Method:
1. Put the value of H.
2. Choose the correct formula.
3. Divide by 11.
4. Convert the mixed fraction into time.

sections.title: Faulty Clock (Fast or Slow Clock)
sections.content:
If a clock gains or loses x minutes in y hours:
Step 1: Error per hour = x/y minutes
Step 2: Total time × error per hour = total error
Step 3: Add or subtract from the correct time

Example:
A clock gains 5 minutes every 2 hours.
After 10 hours:
Error per hour = 5/2 = 2.5 minutes
In 10 hours = 25 minutes fast

If it was correct at 10:00 → It will show 10:25

Reverse Question:
If a clock loses 3 minutes per hour and shows 4:45 after 5 hours
Actual time = 4:45 + (3×5) = 5:00

sections.title: Finding the Day of Any Date (Century Code Method)
sections.content:
Step 1: Remember Century Codes:
1600=6, 1700=4, 1800=2, 1900=0, 2000=6, 2100=4

Step 2: Year Code = (Last two digits + (Last two digits/4))

Step 3: Month Codes (Normal Year):
Jan=0, Feb=3, Mar=3, Apr=6, May=1, Jun=4, Jul=6, Aug=2, Sep=5, Oct=0, Nov=3, Dec=5

Step 4: In a leap year subtract 1 from Jan and Feb

Step 5: Remainder of total sum ÷ 7 = Day

Example: 15 August 1947
Century code (1900)=0
Year code = 47 + 11 = 58
Month code (Aug)=2
Date=15
Total = 0+58+2+15 = 75
75 ÷ 7 = remainder 5
5 = Friday

sections.title: Leap Year Edge Cases
sections.content:
In a leap year, if the date is before 29 February, subtract 1 odd day.
If the date is after it, use normal calculation.

Example:
10 January 2016 (Leap year)
Subtract 1 from the month code because the date is before February.

sections.title: When Does a Calendar Repeat?
sections.content:
A normal year calendar repeats after 6 or 11 years.
A leap year calendar repeats after 28 years.

Reason: 1 normal year = 1 odd day
Leap year = 2 odd days
In 28 years total odd days = 0 (mod 7)

Example:
The calendar of 2015 may repeat in 2026 (after 11 years, check leap years in between).

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content:
Coincide time = 60H/11
Opposite = (60H ± 360)/11
Right angle = (60H ± 180)/11
Faulty clock = total time × error per hour
Day finding = Century + Year + Month + Date ÷ 7
In leap year subtract 1 before February
Leap year calendar repeats after 28 years.

practice_examples.question: When will the hands coincide between 6 and 7?
A clock loses 4 minutes per hour. What will be the difference after 6 hours?
practice_examples.solution_steps:
Step 1: Per hour = 4 minutes
Step 2: 6×4 = 24 minutes
Step 3: 24 minutes slow

practice_examples.question: Find the day on 26 January 1950.
practice_examples.solution_steps:
Step 1: Century code (1900)=0
Step 2: Year code = 50 + 12 = 62
Step 3: Month code (Jan)=0
Step 4: Not a leap year (1950)
Step 5: Total = 0+62+0+26 = 88
88 ÷ 7 = remainder 4
4 = Thursday
